summary:
May 2,  


Well, we got married. Enclosed you will find a little newspaper article on us that appeared last week locally. I sold not only FLOW MY TEARS, THE POLICEMAN SAID to Doubleday but also my newer novel A SCANNER DARKLY as well—I’ve finished the rough draft of it, now. It’s even longer than TEARS. It’s my anti-dope one, and, I think, a very great novel indeed. Tessa feels it to be far and away die best novel I’ve ever done. 

That, really, is just about all the news. The baby is due in mid-July. We’re taking it easy, now, for a while; at last we have plenty of money and have calmed down quite a bit. I meant to say, above, that both novels sold to Doubleday, which is unusual. 
I think my health is improving, since now I am at last under a doctor’s care, along with Tessa. 

Patrice, we have gotten so deep into my work because of SCANNER that we have no other life but our professional one now and our domestic one. The work and the baby: that is all, and it is enough. We are very very happy and full of peace. I am so proud of SCANNER, but more proud of Tessa, who is doing fine. We had a nice wedding, here at the apartment, with Mumm’s champagne and many flowers, and a minister who could not for the life of him remember Tessa’s name. Then afterwards Tessa’s father, who was one of the witnesses, took us out to dinner, a fine dinner that cost a great deal, to his surprise.
